problem: Endgame article did not exist under this title before 2018-12-07 (views = 1-2/day)
action: kept, flagged pre_title_reveal=True, excluded from the trailer window
reason: the 'Avengers: Endgame' title was revealed with the first trailer; earlier traffic went to another page name

problem: AVG_DOOMSDAY_2026: missing calendar days in daily series
action: none to fix
reason: the API returns one row per day; we verify instead of assuming

problem: AVG_ENDGAME_2019: missing calendar days in daily series
action: none to fix
reason: the API returns one row per day; we verify instead of assuming

problem: filmLabel came back as a QID (no English label on Wikidata)
action: title filled from our film key table via the QID
reason: film-name matching: QID is a reliable key

problem: runtime missing for Doomsday (unreleased film)
action: kept as NULL
reason: runtime is not public yet; filling it would be invention

problem: no India-specific release date for Doomsday on Wikidata
action: use 17-Dec-2026 from ThePrint/Sacnilk in the films table, keep Wikidata value NULL
reason: Wikidata only lists the US date (18 Dec); India opens a day earlier

problem: view/like counts stored as text with thousands separators
action: stripped commas, cast to Int64
reason: needed for arithmetic and normalisation

problem: commentCount not available from the watch page
action: kept as NULL (re-run src/collect/youtube_api_collector.py with an API key to fill it)
reason: a missing count is not zero

problem: Dec-2018 Endgame trailers are titled 'Avengers - Official Trailer' (no 'Endgame')
action: matched by rule using the publish year
reason: the title 'Endgame' was revealed inside that trailer

problem: table mixes day rows with 'Week N Collection' and 'Total' rows
action: moved to a separate weekly table
reason: summing day + week rows would double count

problem: currency strings like '₹ 53.60 Cr [En: ...]'
action: parsed to float crore + 4 language columns
reason: type casting text -> numeric

problem: days 15-21 marked '** Approx' by the source
action: kept, flagged is_approx=True
reason: approximate is still the best public figure; flag lets us exclude in robustness checks

problem: language split does not add up to the day total
action: kept day total as the official figure
reason: rounding by the source

problem: days 29-56 only given as 7-day ranges ('Day 29 - Day 35')
action: kept in weekly table only, NOT spread over days
reason: splitting a week evenly would invent a daily pattern

problem: dates as text '26-Apr-2019 (Fri)'
action: parsed with format %d-%b-%Y
reason: text dates -> datetime

problem: Encore late days below ₹0.01 Cr (e.g. '₹0.004 cr.')
action: kept as is (not rounded to 0)
reason: small but real; rounding would create fake zero days

problem: Sacnilk and Bollywood Hungama disagree on some days (e.g. Day 8: 12.00 vs 12.50)
action: keep both columns; primary = Sacnilk where present
reason: Sacnilk gives the language split; disagreement documented, not hidden

problem: days 22-28 missing in Sacnilk (only a Week-4 total)
action: filled from Bollywood Hungama, source column says so
reason: second trade source for the same day is better than a gap

problem: Day 1 reported as 53.10 Cr (BH summary / first Sacnilk estimate) vs 53.60 Cr (both day tables)
reason: day tables are the later, revised figures

problem: only NET is given per day; we need GROSS to compare with Doomsday advance (gross)
action: gross_cr_est = net x 1.2025 (Sacnilk India gross 445.00 / net 370.05)
reason: single published ratio; estimate, clearly labelled _est

problem: Sacnilk page shows two different net totals: 370.05 (summary) and 373.05 (table total)
action: report lifetime as a range (Sacnilk 370.05 / 373.05, BH 373.22), never as one exact number
reason: source inconsistency, documented

problem: BH week 3: days add up to 21.07 but BH weekly table says 21.72
action: kept both; lifetime total taken from published totals, shown as a range
reason: internal inconsistency inside one source

problem: BH week 4: days add up to 8.69 but BH weekly table says 7.59
action: kept both; lifetime total taken from published totals, shown as a range
reason: internal inconsistency inside one source

problem: Sacnilk stops at week 5; BH runs to week 8
action: kept NULL for Sacnilk weeks 6-8
reason: missing in source

problem: 'Lac' and '[without block seats]' mixed into numbers ('2.97 Lac [2.61 Lac]')
action: two numeric columns: with and without block seats; Lac x 1e5
reason: type casting + keep both definitions

problem: 'Others (13 states)' / 'Others (67 cities)' buckets
action: kept, flagged is_others_bucket
reason: needed for totals, but not a real place for ranking

problem: occupancy missing for 'Others' rows and for language rows
action: kept NULL
reason: not published

problem: relative dates like '6 days ago'
action: converted using the access date 2026-11-21
reason: text dates -> datetime; error of +-1 day accepted

problem: IMDb hides all but 5 featured reviews unless you log in
action: used only the 5 public ones; did not log in
reason: assignment rule: never scrape behind a login

problem: no comment files yet (needs a YouTube Data API key)
action: pipeline runs without them; collector script ready in src/collect/
reason: we only use official API for comments

problem:
HTML entities and
tags in text (' ")
action: html.unescape + strip tags
reason: otherwise word counts and sentiment see junk tokens

problem: empty text
action: dropped
reason: nothing to analyse

problem: duplicate review ids
action: dropped
reason: same record collected twice

problem: identical long texts (copy-paste / bot check)
action: kept but flagged is_text_duplicate
reason: short ones like 'masterpiece' repeat naturally; long identical texts would be suspicious

problem: reviews under 3 words ('Masterpiece', 'Peak cinema')
action: kept, flagged is_short
reason: they still carry a star rating; text models may ignore them

problem: non-English reviews (Spanish)
action: kept, flagged lang='es', excluded from English sentiment
reason: VADER / our IMDb-trained model are English-only

problem: no sentiment label on our own reviews
action: derived rating_label from stars (>=7/10 positive, <=4 negative, else mixed)
reason: lets us check the IMDb-50K model on OUR data, not only on its own test split

problem: RT page is shared by the 2019 release and the Sep-2026 Encore re-release
action: viewing_context='encore_rerelease_2026' for reviews dated after 25-Sep-2026
reason: same film key, different moment in time

problem: CPI base changed from 2012=100 to 2024=100 in Feb 2026
action: old-base months multiplied by MoSPI linking factor 0.5267 (Combined)
reason: official linking method; never mix raw 2012-base and 2024-base numbers

problem: overlap check Dec-2025: linked old = 104.29 vs published new = 104.1
action: no change, reported
reason: gap +0.19 points shows the link is approximate (factor is an annual average)

problem: CPI for Nov-2026 not published yet (release 14-Dec-2026)
action: used Oct-2026 CPI (latest available)
reason: one-month gap, effect < 1%

problem: no like-for-like ATP for Endgame 2019 in public sources
action: compare PVR normal ATP 2019 (₹215) with Doomsday advance ATP (₹699), flagged as indicative
reason: CPI is not a cinema price index; we keep the two comparisons separate

problem: duplicate reviews in the 50K corpus
action: dropped
reason: duplicates would leak between train and test

problem: theme keywords are our own dictionary (no labelled theme data)
action: regex dictionary, kept in this file so anyone can audit / change it
reason: transparent > clever for a 145-review sample

problem: Encore has no Wikidata entry of its own
action: genres copied from the parent film (same film + extra scenes), parent_film_id = 1
reason: re-release of the same title

problem: Nov-2026 rows have no CPI month row (not published yet)
action: collection_month = NULL for those rows (FK allows NULL)
reason: keeps referential integrity
